summary: Three well-written passages of real IELTS length (843, 858 and 859 words) whose difficulty rises properly, from a clear history of eyeglasses to a demanding C1 argument about the planning fallacy. The question types and traps are genuine IELTS; the first two passages are a little kinder than the real test, which is right for B2 students. I fixed a question-order error, one question with two possible answers, and one sentence ending that fitted two stems; pair coverage went from 29 to 38 of 40.
strengths: Passage lengths 843/858/859 words; academic magazine register; passage 3 has genuinely C1 vocabulary and argument (inside/outside view, reference-class forecasting).
Good IELTS type mix: sentence completion, TFNG, matching information, summary completion, people matching with an extra name, MCQ, YNNG, sentence endings.
NOT GIVEN items are genuinely unaddressed (guild punishments, contact-lens usage, professions compared), and FALSE/NO items are clearly contradicted.
MCQ distractors echo passage wording (e.g. 'scaled-down', 'possess no information') while the keys paraphrase.

issues.problem: TFNG order broken: Q12's evidence ('still lack the simple spectacles') comes after Q13's ('Contact lenses ... compete for the same eyes') in the last paragraph.
issues.change: Swapped the two statements: Q12 is now the contact-lens NOT GIVEN, Q13 the 'still do not have the glasses' TRUE. Pattern T F NG T F NG T, no runs of three.

issues.problem: 'buildings use less ______ for air conditioning' accepts 'energy' just as well as 'electricity' (paragraph A: 'drives up energy use').
issues.change: Answer is now ['electricity', 'energy']; explain mentions both.

issues.problem: Ending A ('treats a new project as one case within a class of similar ones') describes reference-class forecasting (Q38) even more literally than the outside view, so a student could defensibly put A for Q38.
issues.change: Ending A rewritten to 'relies on information that nearly everyone has but hardly anyone uses.' (only the outside view); Q37 explain/evidence updated.
Now ['a coating of', 'a layer of'], the paraphrase the explanation teaches.

issues.problem: Pair text side 'file away as an exception' not in the passage.
issues.change: Now ['file each one away as an exception', 'every overrun seems exceptional'].

issues.problem: Pair question side 'does not cure' is not in the statement; the same was true of Q19 ('use less electricity'), Q34 ('breaking into parts') and Q24/Q25/Q29/Q31 were weak.
issues.change: All replaced with phrases copied from both sides (e.g. Q32 ['learning from past overruns', 'repeated experience of overruns'], Q34 ['unpack a project into its parts', 'Breaking a project into smaller parts']).

issues.problem: 'had nothing to fix them to the wearer's head' - pinching them onto the nose could be argued as a way of fixing; TRUE is still the best answer (no arms).
issues.change: Optional rewording: 'The earliest spectacles had no side pieces to hold them in place.'

issues.problem: Matching information Q14-18 uses five different paragraphs out of six, one each, so the 'NB any letter more than once' rubric never applies and elimination makes it easier.
issues.change: In a future set, let one paragraph answer two items.
